- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices during sustained upward trends; model tends to lag behind actual momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak to avoid overreaction.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, then undercorrects upward after strong downward moves.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows consistent underestimation of true price volatility; add 5–10% buffer for volatility in high-activity periods.
- When history includes recent high prices, model tends to overestimate future highs; apply downward adjustment of 3–5% for consecutive high values.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the horizon; apply smoothing or exponential decay weighting to early forecast points.
